tooltip.encodedlogistics.info.network_co: The heart of a network. Forms hollow frames up to 7x7x7.
The heart of a network. Touching Network Controllers form one structure: a single block, a line, or the hollow edge frame of a box up to 7x7x7 (a 3x3x3 frame is 20 blocks). Filled faces and anything bigger don't form. Each controller face with a network connection provides 32 lanes. Every block stores 25,000 FE, takes FE on any face, and the network drains 2 FE/t per block plus its devices. Only one controller structure may be on a network.

crt.encodedlogistics.help.main: Type an option's number on the command line and press Enter, or click an option (double-click to go there). Any command can be typed there too: an ELCL command, or a screen's own (WRKLIB, WRKMBR LIB(name), DSPMSG...); F4 prompts it.

crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrklib:
Shows the libraries on this system. Type an option in the Opt column next to a library and press Enter.

  2=Change   Change the text or authority.
  4=Delete   Delete a library you own.
  5=Display  Show its attributes.
  12=Work with members  List the source members.

F6 creates a library (CRTLIB). ELSYS holds the samples and is read-only; ELGPL is for everyone.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrklib.opt: Opt: 2=Change (text, and public authority: *USE lets others read, *CHANGE lets them change members), 4=Delete (asks first), 5=Display, 12=Work with members. Several rows' options are done top to bottom.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.dsplib: A library's attributes: its owner, public authority, how many members it holds and their size. Press Enter or F12 to return.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkmbr:
Shows the source members in a library. Type an option next to a member and press Enter.

  2=Edit     Open it in the source editor.
  3=Copy     Copy it to another library or name.
  4=Delete   Delete it (asks first).
  5=Display  Show it, read-only.
  6=Print    Print the source to Work with Output.
  7=Rename   Give it a new name.
  14=Compile Create its program; the listing goes to Work with Output.

Chg * means the source changed after it was compiled. F6 creates a member, F11 sorts.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkmbr.opt: Opt: 2=Edit, 3=Copy, 4=Delete, 5=Display, 6=Print, 7=Rename, 14=Compile. In ELSYS only 3, 5, 6 and 14 (into a library of yours) work: it's read-only.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.cmdent: Type any ELCL command and press Enter: it runs in your interactive job and its messages show here (ID and text), with the values its RTN parameters return. F4 prompts the command on the command line, Tab completes its last word, F9 brings back earlier commands, F13 clears this list.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkinv: The network's items, hot and on tape. Type an option next to an item: 1=Withdraw, 5=Display details, 7=Craft. Position to: the starting characters of a name. F6 puts items from your inventory in. F11 sorts by name, quantity or mod.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkinv.opt: Opt: 1=Withdraw (to the desk drawer or your inventory), 5=Display details, 7=Craft (items a schematic makes).
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkcrfjob: The network's crafting jobs. 4=Cancel (Enter again to confirm), 5=Display its steps. Refreshes every two seconds. F10 shows the jobs that ended (the last CRFLOGRTN of them, newest first): 4=Remove, 5=Display the record (what it made, why it failed, who asked, the ingredients used), 7=Craft again; F11 sorts by ended time, item or status. F10 again goes back.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkcrfjob.posi: Position to: the starting characters of an item's name; only ended jobs for those items show (blank or *ALL: all).
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkdev: Every device on the network, with its lanes and status. 2=Change its name, 5=Display its details, 8=Locate it in the world. Scripts name devices by the name shown first in the Device column (CTLIF01, UPS01...): given once when the device first joins a network (its type and the lowest number free), kept with the device until it's renamed.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkdev.opt: Opt: 2=Change (rename), 5=Display, 8=Locate (a box blinks around it for ten seconds).
crt.encodedlogistics.help.dspnetsts: Storage, energy, lanes, crafting and devices at a glance. Refreshes every two seconds. Press Enter to return.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.morekeys: Every key the screens take, and this terminal's phosphor: Green, Amber, White, or *SYSVAL to follow the system's PHOSPHOR value.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.prompt: Type a value in each field and press Enter. F4 lists a field's values, F10 shows the additional parameters, F5 resets them, F12 returns without the command.

crt.encodedlogistics.help.edtmbr:
The source editor. Type over a line's text to change it; type a line command over its sequence number and press Enter:

  I, In   insert 1 / n lines after
  D, Dn   delete 1 / n lines
  DD..DD  delete a block
  C, CC..CC  copy, M, MM..MM  move: then A (after) or B (before) a line
  R, Rn   repeat the line
  X, Xn   exclude lines (S or F shows them)
  COLS    the column ruler

On the command line: FIND, CHANGE, TOP, BOTTOM, SAVE, FILE (save and exit), CANCEL, RESET, or any ELCL command (F4 prompts it). Enter checks the changed statements; the first bad one shows reversed with its message. F4 on a source line prompts its statement; F11 edits full screen; F19 / F20 shift the columns shown.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.edtmbr.margin: The sequence number (0012.00). Type a line command over it: I, D, DD, C, CC, M, MM, A, B, R, X, S or F (with a count where it takes one), or COLS; Enter applies them all, top to bottom. A copy or move waits ("Block command pending") until it has its target; F12 or RESET drops it.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.edtmbr.text: The line's text (72 of its 80 columns; F19 / F20 shift them). Type over it; the Insert key switches to inserting. F4 here prompts the statement that starts on this line and writes the answer back, continued with + where it's long.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrksplf:
Your spooled output: compile listings, printed members, PRTTXT text, job logs. Type an option next to a file:

  4=Delete   Delete it (asks first).
  5=Display  Show it.
  6=Print    Print it on the Line Printer.

F11 sorts by created, file or status.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.dspsplf: A spooled file, a page at a time: PageUp / PageDown roll it, F19 / F20 shift the columns by 40 (a compile listing's change dates are past column 80).
crt.encodedlogistics.help.dspsplf.contro: Control: +n or -n lines, T for the top, B for the bottom, or a page number; press Enter.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.dspsplf.find: Find: text to look for from the line after the top one (any case); press Enter.

crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkactjob:
The system's script jobs: the interactive one of each terminal session and the batch jobs on the job hosts. Type an option next to a job:

  2=Change   Its priority and command logging.
  3=Hold     Hold it.
  4=End      End it (asks first; F11 there ends it at once).
  5=Work with  Its menu: status, definition, log, call stack.
  6=Release  Release a held job.
  8=Spooled files  Its output.

Budget: how much of its per-tick budget it used. F5 refreshes and starts Elapsed again; F11 sorts.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkjob: A job's menu. Type a number on the command line and press Enter (or click one): 1 its status, 2 its definition, 4 its spooled files, 10 its log, 11 the programs it's running, 30 all of them one after another.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.dspjob: A job's attributes. Press Enter or F12 to return.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.dspjoblog: A job's log, newest at the bottom: the commands it ran (>>, when it logs them) and every message it got, with its ID. F10 shows each message's details; PageUp / PageDown roll it.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrkjobscde:
Jobs submitted on a schedule (game clock times, real-time intervals). Type an option next to an entry:

  2=Change      Prompt it with its values.
  3=Hold        Hold it (again: release it).
  4=Remove      Remove it (asks first).
  10=Submit now Run its command now; the entry stays.

F6 adds an entry (ADDJOBSCDE).
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrktrgevt:
Programs run when something happens in the network: an item's count crossing a value, storage filling, a device faulting, the power switching to UPS, a craft ending, a Control Interface's redstone changing. Type an option next to a trigger:

  2=Change   Prompt it with its values.
  3=Hold     Hold it (again: release it).
  4=Remove   Remove it (asks first).

F6 adds one (ADDTRGEVT).
crt.encodedlogistics.help.dspmsg: Your message queue, newest first: what your jobs and other users sent you. Unread ones are bright; showing them here marks them read and MW goes from the message line. 4=Remove, 5=Display details. F11 removes them all.
crt.encodedlogistics.help.dspmsg.opt: Opt: 4=Remove, 5=Display details (the whole text, its ID, severity, sender and time).
crt.encodedlogistics.help.wrksysval: The system's values (SYSNAME, DATFMT, SECLVL, QMAXJOB, LOGRTN, PHOSPHOR). 2=Change one (a security officer only), 5=Display it with its default and allowed values. PHOSPHOR is every terminal's colour unless a player picked their own (F24=More keys).
